From 33c1c6d8a28a2761ac74b0380b2563cf546c2a3a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Guangshuo Li <lgs201920130244@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 21:32:35 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] powerpc/smp: Add check for kcalloc() failure in
 parse_thread_groups()

As kcalloc() may fail, check its return value to avoid a NULL pointer
dereference when passing it to of_property_read_u32_array().

Fixes: 790a1662d3a26 ("powerpc/smp: Parse ibm,thread-groups with multiple properties")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@csgroup.eu>
Signed-off-by: Guangshuo Li <lgs201920130244@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Madhavan Srinivasan <maddy@linux.ibm.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20250923133235.1862108-1-lgs201920130244@gmail.com

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/kernel/smp.c b/arch/powerpc/kernel/smp.c
index 292fee8809bc..cad3358fa4c3 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/kernel/smp.c
+++ b/arch/powerpc/kernel/smp.c
@@ -822,6 +822,8 @@ static int parse_thread_groups(struct device_node *dn,
 
 	count = of_property_count_u32_elems(dn, "ibm,thread-groups");
 	thread_group_array = kcalloc(count, sizeof(u32), GFP_KERNEL);
+	if (!thread_group_array)
+		return -ENOMEM;
 	ret = of_property_read_u32_array(dn, "ibm,thread-groups",
 					 thread_group_array, count);
 	if (ret)
-- 
2.34.1

In `arch/powerpc/kernel/smp.c`, the function `parse_thread_groups()` now includes a check for the return value of `kcalloc()`. If the allocation fails, the function returns `-ENOMEM` immediately, preventing a NULL pointer from being passed to `of_property_read_u32_array()`. This avoids a potential NULL pointer dereference and subsequent crash.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
thread_group_array = kcalloc(count, sizeof(u32), GFP_KERNEL);
ret = of_property_read_u32_array(dn, "ibm,thread-groups",
				 thread_group_array, count);
Reason:
kcalloc() can fail and return NULL if memory allocation fails. Without a NULL check, the code unconditionally passes the uninitialized thread_group_array pointer to of_property_read_u32_array(), which dereferences it, causing a NULL pointer dereference and a crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
+	if (!thread_group_array)
+		return -ENOMEM;
Reason:
Adding a check for the return value of kcalloc() ensures that if allocation fails, the function returns an appropriate error code (-ENOMEM) instead of proceeding with a NULL pointer. This prevents the NULL pointer dereference in the subsequent call to of_property_read_u32_array().
